introduction: The Báb’s first book promised an ark “crimson-coloured” for “the people of Bahá”, and Bahá’u’lláh’s writings return to the image constantly: the Crimson Ark has sailed, those who recognize Him are its companions, no storm can sink it. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá applies it to the Covenant, “the Ark of Salvation”. This guide gathers such passages, most of them a single line. The first ark is Noah’s, in Genesis and in the Qur’an, where the command is “Embark therein!” and a son who trusts a mountain is drowned; the Gospels add the boat in the storm and Peter sinking when he looked at the wind, and Acts has Paul’s “except these abide in the ship”. Because the image sorts people into the saved and the drowned, Peter’s “God is no respecter of persons” and the Qur’an’s promise to all who believe and do right are placed beside reading 59.
questions: What does the image of an ark say about a religious community that images like “garden” or “city” do not?
Peter began to sink “when he saw the wind boisterous”. What is the equivalent in the readings of looking at the wind?
Reading 59 sees those who turned away as “drowned”. How should such language be held together with “God is no respecter of persons”?
Most of these readings simply tell someone they are aboard. What would that assurance have meant to a persecuted believer?

outside.why: “This is the Ark of God.” The first ark: come thou and all thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.
By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, prepared an ark to the saving of his house.
The world an ocean, and the Covenant the Ark of Salvation. Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast.
Follow the Navigator. They that go down to the sea in ships, that do business in great waters; these see the works of the Lord, and his wonders in the deep.
Stand firm though all in heaven and earth war against thee. Milton’s Abdiel: among innumerable false, unmoved, unshaken, unseduced, unterrified.
“If I were to hesitate at the sight of every danger.” Peter walked on the water; but when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid, and began to sink.
The tempest was violent, and the Ark reached safety. He arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still.
Paul to the soldiers in the storm: except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.
“The Crimson Ark hath sailed.” Noah in the Qur’an: embark therein! In the name of Allah be its course and its mooring.
Enter, O people of Bahá. When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee.
Whoever recognizes God today is recorded as one of the people of the Ark. Another book was opened, which is the book of life.
The fear of God, fountain-head of goodly deeds. The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.
Victory through patience in times of trial. Behold, we count them happy which endure.
The censure of deniers has not kept them back. Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness’ sake.
Be not grieved by what has befallen you. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer.
They have embarked and detached themselves from all else. Behold, we have forsaken all, and followed thee.

However high the waves of tests, they will not reach the Ark’s passengers. The rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.
Therefore will not we fear, though the waters thereof roar and be troubled.
The people of Bahá in the Ark, and those who turned away drowned. Noah’s son in the Qur’an: I shall betake me to some mountain. And the wave came in between them, so he was among the drowned.

The image divides humanity into those aboard and those lost. Peter learned something that strains every such image: God is no respecter of persons: but in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him. How do you read reading 59 beside the Bahá’í teaching that all peoples are one?

The Qur’an, whose ark this is, also says: those who believe, and those who are Jews, and Christians, and Sabaeans, whoever believeth in Allah and the Last Day and doeth right, surely their reward is with their Lord.
Soon every soul returns to its place. As it was in the days of Noe: they did eat, they drank, they married wives, until the day that Noah entered into the ark.
Oceans tinged crimson around the Gate. The children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground. Why do stories of rescue through water recur in every scripture?

shortfall: Forty of the sixty-three readings are one sentence in slightly different words (“such a one is of the companions of the Crimson Ark mentioned in the Qayyúmu’l-Asmá’”); a companion was given to each distinct statement about the Ark and none to the repetitions.

matthew-peter-walked-on-the-water.text: And he said, Come. And when Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the water, to go to Jesus. But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me. And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him, and said unto him, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt

genesis-come-thou-into-the-ark.text: And the Lord said unto Noah, Come thou and all thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation

quran-embark-therein.text: And he said: Embark therein! In the name of Allah be its course and its mooring. Lo! my Lord is Forgiving, Merciful.

quran-none-that-saveth-this-day.text: He said: I shall betake me to some mountain that will save me from the water. (Noah) said: This day there is none that saveth from the commandment of Allah save him on whom He hath had mercy. And the wave came in between them, so he was among the drowned.
